org.name: Meridian Data
org.description: A ~250-person software vendor selling a cloud data platform. Engineering works in a Go/TypeScript monorepo driven by an internal build CLI (merc), ships behind a feature-flag/config service (Beacon), designs through an RFC-and-service-catalog system (Atlas), queries an internal warehouse with a CLI (mq), runs incidents on Sentinel with runbooks, builds and deploys through Forge CI/CD, styles UI with the Compass design system, bills through Ledger, observes with Pulse, and grounds answers in the Nexus internal-docs RAG.

techniques.name: Query the warehouse with mq instead of pasting rows
techniques.description: Pasting exported rows into the prompt is lossy and stale. The internal `mq` CLI lets the agent query the warehouse directly, so it works from live, complete data.

triggers.heuristic: user pastes tabular rows or CSV exported from the warehouse

techniques.applies_when: The question is about data that lives in the Meridian warehouse and the user has pasted or described rows by hand.
techniques.not_when: The data is not in the warehouse, or the user needs a one-off value they already have in front of them.
techniques.recipe: Run `mq query "SELECT ... FROM <table> WHERE ..."` against the warehouse and reason from the result set, instead of pasting rows. Use `mq schema <table>` first if you're unsure of the columns.
techniques.before_after: Before: a truncated CSV paste and guesses about the schema. After: a live `mq` query over the real table.

techniques.name: Scaffold a new service with merc new
techniques.description: Hand-writing service boilerplate drifts from the monorepo's conventions. `merc new service` generates a service that already wires up config, logging, health checks and CI.

triggers.heuristic: user is creating a new service or package from scratch in the monorepo

techniques.applies_when: The user is starting a new service or component inside the Meridian monorepo.
techniques.not_when: The work is a change to an existing service rather than a new one.
techniques.recipe: Run `merc new service <name>` (or `merc new lib <name>`) to scaffold from the golden template, then fill in the handlers. Don't hand-copy another service's boilerplate.
techniques.before_after: Before: copied boilerplate that missed the new health-check contract. After: a `merc`-scaffolded service that passed CI on the first push.

techniques.name: Check Beacon flag state before chasing a config bug
techniques.description: Behaviour that differs by environment is usually a feature flag, not a code bug. Reading the Beacon flag state first avoids a fruitless code hunt.

triggers.heuristic: a bug reproduces in one environment but not another

techniques.applies_when: A behaviour differs between environments or users and the code path looks identical.
techniques.not_when: The failure is a hard crash or compile error unrelated to configuration.
techniques.recipe: Run `beacon get <flag>` / `beacon eval <flag> --context <env-or-user>` to see the resolved flag state for the failing case before reading code. Compare the resolved values across the environments that differ.
techniques.before_after: Before: an afternoon reading request handlers. After: `beacon eval` showed the flag was off in prod.

techniques.name: Draft an Atlas RFC from the golden template
techniques.description: A blank doc invites an off-format RFC that review bounces. Generating from the Atlas template gets the required sections (context, options, risks, rollout) right the first time.

triggers.heuristic: user is writing a design proposal or RFC for a non-trivial change

techniques.applies_when: The user is proposing a design that warrants an Atlas RFC.
techniques.not_when: The change is small enough to ship without an RFC.
techniques.recipe: Run `atlas rfc new <slug>` to open the templated doc, then fill each section from the change at hand. Keep the Options and Rollback sections — review checks for them.

techniques.name: Pull the Sentinel runbook into context during an incident
techniques.description: Under incident pressure people improvise steps that a runbook already documents. Loading the Sentinel runbook keeps mitigation on the vetted path.

triggers.heuristic: an active incident or alert is being worked

techniques.applies_when: The user is mitigating an active incident that has a Sentinel runbook.
techniques.not_when: There is no incident, or the service has no runbook yet.
techniques.recipe: Run `sentinel runbook <service>` and follow the documented mitigation and rollback steps. Paste the alert into the session so the agent maps it to the right runbook section.
techniques.before_after: Before: an improvised rollback that made the blast radius worse. After: the runbook's documented drain-then-rollback sequence.

techniques.name: Ground the answer in Nexus internal docs
techniques.description: A model's generic answer misses Meridian's own conventions. Retrieving from Nexus (the internal-docs RAG) grounds the answer in how we actually do it here.

triggers.heuristic: user asks how something works at the company, not in general

techniques.applies_when: The question is about a Meridian-specific convention, process, or system.
techniques.not_when: The question is about a public technology with no internal specifics.
techniques.recipe: Query Nexus with `nexus ask "<question>"` (or attach the returned doc IDs) and answer from the retrieved internal docs, citing them, rather than from general knowledge.

techniques.name: Generate a Forge pipeline from the golden config
techniques.description: Copy-pasted CI drifts from the current Forge schema and fails opaquely. Generating from the golden config gets caching, required checks and deploy gates right.
techniques.applies_when: The user is adding or fixing a Forge CI pipeline for a service.
techniques.not_when: The CI system in question is not Forge.
techniques.recipe: Run `forge init --from golden` to emit a current pipeline, then adapt the build/test/deploy stages. Validate with `forge lint` before pushing.

techniques.name: Reason about billing with the Ledger glossary
techniques.description: Billing terms (proration, entitlement, dunning) mean specific things in Ledger. Loading the glossary keeps the agent from applying textbook definitions that don't match our model.
techniques.applies_when: The task touches billing, invoicing, or entitlements in the Ledger service.
techniques.not_when: The work is unrelated to billing.
techniques.recipe: Attach the Ledger domain glossary (`nexus ask "ledger glossary <term>"`) and reason with Meridian's definitions of proration, entitlement and dunning, not generic ones.

techniques.name: Build UI from Compass primitives, not raw markup
techniques.description: Hand-rolled markup ignores Compass tokens and accessibility rules and fails design review. Composing from Compass primitives ships consistent, accessible UI.

triggers.heuristic: user is writing UI markup or styling by hand

techniques.applies_when: The user is building UI in a surface that uses the Compass design system.
techniques.not_when: The surface predates Compass or is a throwaway prototype.
techniques.recipe: Compose from Compass components (`<Compass.Button>`, `<Compass.Field>`, tokens) rather than raw HTML/CSS. Import from `@meridian/compass` and use the documented props.

techniques.name: Add Pulse SLO instrumentation to a new service
techniques.description: A service that ships without SLOs is invisible until it pages someone. Wiring Pulse SLOs at build time means it's observable on day one.
techniques.applies_when: The user is adding or reviewing a service that lacks SLO instrumentation.
techniques.not_when: The service already has Pulse SLOs defined.
techniques.recipe: Add a `pulse.slo.yaml` from the template and instrument the golden signals with the Pulse SDK. Run `pulse validate` to confirm the SLOs register.

techniques.name: Write a warehouse migration the Helios way
techniques.description: Ad-hoc DDL against the warehouse skips Helios's backfill and reversibility guarantees. Generating a Helios migration makes the change safe to roll forward and back.
techniques.applies_when: The user is changing warehouse schema managed by Helios.
techniques.not_when: The schema is outside Helios's control.
techniques.recipe: Run `helios migration new <name>`, write the forward and reverse steps, and include a backfill plan. Never hand-run DDL against the warehouse.
techniques.before_after: Before: a manual ALTER that couldn't be rolled back. After: a reversible Helios migration with a backfill step.

techniques.name: Run the internal threat-model checklist on a change
techniques.description: Security-relevant changes slip through without a structured review. The internal threat-model checklist surfaces authz, data-handling and secrets issues before merge.
techniques.applies_when: The change touches auth, secrets, PII, or a trust boundary.
techniques.not_when: The change has no security surface.
techniques.recipe: Pull the checklist with `sentinel threat-model` and walk the change against each item (authz, input validation, secret handling, data classification). Record the answers in the PR.

techniques.name: Trace service dependencies with the Atlas service map
techniques.description: Guessing what calls a service leads to missed blast radius. The Atlas service map shows the real upstream and downstream dependencies.
techniques.applies_when: The user needs to know what depends on a service before changing it.
techniques.not_when: The dependency graph is already known and small.
techniques.recipe: Run `atlas deps <service>` (or open its Atlas page) to list upstreams and downstreams before making a breaking change, and check owners for each.

techniques.name: Find latency with Pulse distributed traces
techniques.description: Latency debugging by reading code guesses at the hot path. A Pulse trace shows exactly which span dominates the request.

triggers.heuristic: user is investigating a slow request or endpoint

techniques.applies_when: The user is debugging latency in a Pulse-instrumented service.
techniques.not_when: The service isn't instrumented, or the problem isn't latency.
techniques.recipe: Pull a representative trace with `pulse trace <request-id>` and find the dominant span before touching code. Optimize the span that actually owns the time.

techniques.name: Estimate warehouse query cost before running it
techniques.description: A careless warehouse query can scan terabytes and cost real money. Estimating first catches the expensive full-scan before it runs.
techniques.applies_when: The user is about to run a large or unbounded warehouse query.
techniques.not_when: The query is small and bounded.
techniques.recipe: Run `mq explain --cost "<query>"` first; if it scans more than a few GB, add partitions/filters before running it for real.

techniques.name: Migrate legacy YAML config to Beacon
techniques.description: Hand-editing legacy YAML config keeps drift alive. Converting it to Beacon-managed flags makes the config auditable and safe to change at runtime.
techniques.applies_when: The user is touching a service still on legacy YAML config.
techniques.not_when: The config already lives in Beacon.
techniques.recipe: Run `beacon import <path/to/config.yaml>` to stage the flags, review the mapping, then delete the YAML and read via the Beacon SDK.

techniques.name: Draft a customer postmortem from the Sentinel timeline
techniques.description: A postmortem written from memory misses steps and timings. Building it from the Sentinel incident timeline produces an accurate, customer-ready writeup.
techniques.applies_when: The user is writing a postmortem for a resolved incident that has a Sentinel timeline.
techniques.not_when: There is no recorded incident timeline.
techniques.recipe: Export the timeline with `sentinel timeline <incident-id>` and draft the postmortem into the customer template: impact, timeline, root cause, and follow-ups tied to the recorded events.

techniques.name: Run the mobile release runbook
techniques.description: Mobile releases have store-specific steps that are easy to skip. The internal release runbook keeps staged rollout, changelog and rollback in order.
techniques.applies_when: The user is cutting a mobile app release.
techniques.not_when: The change isn't a mobile release.
techniques.recipe: Open `atlas runbook mobile-release` and walk the staged-rollout, changelog, and rollback steps. Confirm the phased-rollout percentage before submitting to the stores.

techniques.name: Find the right reviewers from Atlas CODEOWNERS
techniques.description: Tagging the wrong reviewers stalls a PR. Atlas resolves the owning team and the humans who actually review that path.
techniques.applies_when: The user is opening a PR and needs the correct reviewers.
techniques.not_when: The reviewers are already known and correct.
techniques.recipe: Run `atlas owners <path>` to resolve the owning team and suggested reviewers for the files you changed, and request those rather than guessing.

techniques.name: Reproduce a data bug with a warehouse snapshot
techniques.description: Debugging a data bug against live tables is nondeterministic. A pinned warehouse snapshot makes the repro stable and shareable.
techniques.applies_when: The user is chasing a data discrepancy that's hard to reproduce against live data.
techniques.not_when: The bug isn't data-dependent.
techniques.recipe: Pin a snapshot with `mq snapshot <table> --as-of <ts>` and reproduce against it, so the failing rows stay fixed while you debug.

techniques.name: Summarize an ADR from Nexus before a design review
techniques.description: Walking into a design review without the prior decisions repeats settled debates. A Nexus ADR summary brings the context in fast.
techniques.applies_when: The user is preparing for a design review of an area with existing ADRs.
techniques.not_when: There are no relevant ADRs.
techniques.recipe: Ask Nexus for the area's ADRs (`nexus ask "ADRs for <area>"`) and summarize the decisions and their rationale before the review, so you don't reopen settled ones.

techniques.name: Ship a hotfix with the legacy deploy.sh
techniques.description: For urgent hotfixes people reach for the old deploy.sh because it's familiar. It skips the Forge migration and canary gates, so it often trades a fast push now for a follow-on incident later — which is why its helped rate stays stubbornly low.
techniques.applies_when: The user wants to push an urgent change and reaches for the legacy deploy path.
techniques.not_when: A normal Forge deploy is available and there's no time pressure.
techniques.recipe: Run `./deploy.sh <service> <env>` to push directly. (Prefer `forge deploy` — it runs the migration and canary gates the script skips.)
techniques.before_after: Before: a fast direct push. After: a skipped migration gate that caused a follow-on incident.

techniques.name: Prove a new test fails without the fix
techniques.description: A green suite can be green for the wrong reason. Before trusting a new test, make it fail on purpose so you know it actually guards the behaviour.
techniques.applies_when: The user just added a test alongside a fix.
techniques.not_when: The test was already shown to fail without the fix.
techniques.recipe: Revert the fix in place, run the new test, and confirm it fails with a message that names the real defect. Restore the fix and confirm it passes.

techniques.name: Get a written plan before a large multi-file edit
techniques.description: Diving straight into a big change produces sprawling diffs that are hard to review. A short plan first keeps the change scoped and reviewable.
techniques.applies_when: The user is about to make a change spanning many files or systems.
techniques.not_when: The change is small and local.
techniques.recipe: Ask for a short step-by-step plan (files to touch, order, risks) and approve it before any edits. Keep the plan in the session as the checklist.

techniques.name: Paste the full stack trace, not your paraphrase
techniques.description: A paraphrased error drops the frames and values that locate the bug. The full trace lets the agent read the actual failure.

triggers.heuristic: user describes an error in prose instead of pasting it

techniques.applies_when: The user is debugging a failure they've described rather than pasted.
techniques.not_when: The full error is already in the session.
techniques.recipe: Paste the complete stack trace and the command that produced it, unabridged, before asking for a diagnosis.

techniques.name: Capture on-call tribal knowledge as a runbook
techniques.description: The fix an on-call engineer just worked out lives only in their head and Slack. Capturing it as a Sentinel runbook makes it reusable next time.
techniques.applies_when: An on-call engineer just resolved something that isn't documented.
techniques.not_when: A runbook already covers the situation.
techniques.recipe: After mitigating, run `sentinel runbook new <service>` and write up the symptom, the check, and the fix you just used, so the next on-call finds it.

techniques.name: Generate Terraform for a service from its Atlas spec
techniques.description: Hand-writing infra for a new service drifts from the standards Atlas already knows. Generating Terraform from the Atlas spec keeps tags, networking and IAM to policy.
techniques.applies_when: The user is provisioning infra for a service that has an Atlas spec.
techniques.not_when: The infra already exists and is compliant.
techniques.recipe: Run `atlas infra gen <service>` to emit Terraform from the service's Atlas spec, then review the IAM and networking blocks against policy before applying.
